facts.raw_span: 2-year history of gradual-onset right facial weakness leading to paralysis
denied hearing loss, tinnitus, imbalance, or other cranial nerve deficits
complete right facial paralysis
nonpulsatile mass protruding through the inferior ear canal
mild sensorineural loss at 4000 Hz
5 × 10-mm irregular lesion in the right mastoid near the stylomastoid foramen
heterogeneous enhancement on T1 with contrast
expansion of the fallopian canal distal to the second genu of the facial nerve
erosion of the posterior external auditory canal
expansion of the stylomastoid foramen
Pleomorphic hyperchromatic nuclei, staining positive for S100 and negative for KI-67
Low cellularity and low MIB-1 proliferation index

concepts.why: The presence of a nonpulsatile mass protruding through the inferior ear canal, a 5 × 10-mm irregular lesion in the right mastoid near the stylomastoid foramen, and expansion of the fallopian canal distal to the second genu of the facial nerve, along with the histopathological findings of pleomorphic hyperchromatic nuclei staining positive for S100, are consistent with a diagnosis of facial nerve schwannoma.
It explains the heterogeneous enhancement on T1 with contrast due to the cartilaginous nature of the tumor.

rationales.F01: Gradual-onset facial weakness is consistent with a slow-growing tumor like facial nerve schwannoma.
rationales.F04: A nonpulsatile mass protruding through the inferior ear canal is highly suggestive of a tumor, such as facial nerve schwannoma.
rationales.F06: The presence of an irregular lesion in the right mastoid near the stylomastoid foramen is consistent with facial nerve schwannoma.
rationales.F08: Expansion of the fallopian canal distal to the second genu of the facial nerve is consistent with facial nerve schwannoma.
rationales.F09: Erosion of the posterior external auditory canal is consistent with an aggressive tumor, but can be seen in both facial nerve schwannoma and chondrosarcoma.
rationales.F10: Expansion of the stylomastoid foramen is consistent with facial nerve schwannoma.
rationales.F11: Pleomorphic hyperchromatic nuclei staining positive for S100 are characteristic of schwannomas, including facial nerve schwannoma.
rationales.F12: Low cellularity and low MIB-1 proliferation index are more consistent with a benign tumor like facial nerve schwannoma.
